## Body

PASS-WITH-NOTES at fe67c7e26d89c3abbc18b5cd139f77714fba56c1, final round under C34.

The two original witnesses are closed at this head:
- B320-01: review_f268_failed_renewal_must_not_restart_a_live_receiver_before_retry
  now queues ZERO controls after a mechanical renewal whose audit append failed.
  on_lapse's new current-daemon lease brake spares it despite the stale spine.
  Dropping that brake restores ONE restart and fails the original oracle.
- B320-02: review_second_expiry_after_failed_renewal now yields TWO lapse edges
  and ONE restart after the prior acting window expired. Keeping renewal debt
  apart from native_lapsed preserves the second real loss. Re-marking native_lapsed
  on a failed renewal restores ONE edge / ZERO controls and fails the oracle.
- The original next-heartbeat retry control passes; dropping renewal debt on
  failure kills it. Held bodies still return once, new live sends are not parked,
  and the held-decision window, gap catch-up and prompt-abort controls pass.

The new brake is a BRAKE, not a replacement POLICY: it only spares, and a failed
lease read spares without recording a decision. The debt set is keyed by seat,
removed after successful audit and pruned with the existing live-native roster;
it no longer authorizes lapse-edge suppression.

New notes owed (C34 follow-ups, not regressions introduced by R2):

N320-R2-01 — startup protection is ordering-dependent, not durable.
The current-daemon lease proof is deliberately not restored from the stale
spine. Replacing the delivery service with a fresh one on the same real
registry/queue/spine after an unrecorded renewal gives a boot-grace live receiver
but native_receiver_renewed=false: reconcile queues ONE restart. If that receiver
heartbeats with the new service first (and its new audit also fails), reconcile
queues ZERO. Thus a healthy extension whose reattachment/heartbeat loses the
boot race is not covered merely by delivery's boot grace.
The exclusion preserves F261's required recovery of a genuinely lost extension
at attachment; counting every boot-grace seat as renewed would suppress it.
Initial native attestation/registration also initializes the lease entry, so
reattachment can supply the brake before the first heartbeat; the helper means
"current matching lease entry", not literally "a heartbeat was observed".
Sources: delivery/mod.rs:417-427,639-679,783-796.
Name this startup tradeoff explicitly; a future ordering change must keep the
existing pre-attachment lost-extension control. The probe reconstructs the
service state, not a real daemon bounce, which was forbidden.

N320-R2-02 — the lease brake is one snapshot before awaited decision work.
on_lapse checks the lease and releases native_lock before handle obtains/uses
the per-seat ledger and awaits liveness/composer/store work
(auth_recovery.rs:721-733,260-339; delivery/mod.rs:783-796).
A deterministic LivenessPort latch held a decision AFTER the brake had returned
false. While held, the registered receiver renewed, its audit failed, and the
current lease read became true. Releasing liveness still produced Action::Restart
and ONE queued control. This is not covered by a before-call brake test, and it
also existed without R2's brake. Any future final-check/serialization repair
must respect the native-lock/control-admission lock order, not simply hold the
global native mutex across the whole recovery handler.
These two newly characterized boundaries do not negate the GREEN original
orderings, but they prohibit a blanket all-interleaving or post-bounce claim.

Merge, identity and cost:
- The final merge preserves the R2 production hunks. Its inherited TapAttach
  signature adjustment matches main's port change; diff whitespace check passes.
  The reviewer checkout is detached and unchanged.
- The brake matches the current registry incarnation's PID, process start and
  native session, then its in-memory lease age, under native_lock. A previous
  incarnation's lease cannot supply this proof. It grants no new sender authority.
- No new timer, subscriber, task or process launch. One extra registry call and
  lease lookup per eligible lapse check; gap reconciliation is bounded to once
  per ten seconds after completion, not heartbeat/live-event throughput.
- As performance noted, every renewing heartbeat also checks the owed set;
  default lease/3 recommends twenty seconds, not a server-side rate cap. The
  existing receiver reconciliation prunes the new set by roster membership,
  potentially O(owed entries * live Copilot roster) comparisons. Audit-only
  retries no longer repeat successful held-body recovery; return-stage failure
  still can. No measured live CPU-saving claim is made.
